subject: Chemistry
title: YInMn Blue: A New Blue Pigment
description: A quick, practical guide to YInMn Blue: A New Blue Pigment.

hook.text: In 2009, a chemistry student accidentally created the first new blue pigment in over 200 years. It's called YInMn blue.

buildup.text: Andrew Smith was heating yttrium, indium, and manganese oxides at Oregon State. The sample came out of the furnace vivid blue.

discovery.text: Manganese ions in the crystal absorb red and green light. The structure is so stable the color never fades.

twist.text: YInMn blue reflects infrared heat. Buildings painted with it stay cooler—it's a pigment that saves energy.

climax.text: Crayola added it as a crayon color in 2017 called 'Bluetiful.' A lab accident became a household name.

punchline.text: A lab accident at 1,200°C. The newest blue pigment in two centuries.

quiz.question: What unexpected property does YInMn blue have?
options: It reflects infrared heat, keeping painted surfaces cooler
It glows in the dark without any external energy
It changes color depending on temperature

details.summary: YInMn Blue was accidentally discovered by chemist Mas Subramanian in 2009 while researching electronic materials. The pigment, containing yttrium, indium, and manganese oxides, produces a vivid blue through manganese's electronic transitions in a trigonal bipyramidal crystal structure.
details.whyItMatters: YInMn Blue is the first new blue pigment discovered in over two centuries. Its non-toxic composition and exceptional durability make it significant for sustainable pigment development.
takeaways: YInMn Blue was accidentally found during electronics materials research
Manganese in a trigonal bipyramidal structure creates the blue color
It is non-toxic, fade-resistant, and reflects infrared heat effectively

faq.question: Why is discovering a new blue pigment considered significant?
faq.answer: Blue pigments have historically been rare and difficult to produce. The last major blue discoveries were cobalt blue in 1802 and synthetic ultramarine in 1828. Finding a new, non-toxic, durable blue expands options for art, industry, and sustainable manufacturing.

faq.question: How does YInMn Blue help with building energy efficiency?
faq.answer: YInMn Blue reflects infrared radiation while absorbing visible blue wavelengths. Buildings and vehicles coated with it stay cooler in sunlight because the pigment does not absorb heat-producing infrared energy. This property could reduce air conditioning energy consumption significantly.
